description:
Error::ProfileViolation::reason and Error::OcspDelegation::reason both carry the same lengthy rustdoc explaining why the field is Cow<'static, str> rather than &'static str (lines 175-180 and 204-208). The rationale is verbatim duplicated:

    `Cow<'static, str>` rather than `&'static str` so the serde
    deserialize path can yield an owned `String` without leaking
    memory. Producers always supply `Cow::Borrowed` from a
    `&'static str` literal; the `Cow::Owned` variant arises only
    on the deserialize path.

This is the type-level invariant of 'all our static-string error reasons are Cow'. If a future variant adds another such field, the rationale will be duplicated a third time, or worse, will drift.

SUGGESTED REWRITE: hoist the rationale to a module-level doc comment on Error itself (near line 147 where Error is declared), then have each variant's reason field point at it:

    /// Fixed-string description of which invariant was violated.
    /// See the [] type docs for why this is .
    reason: Cow<'static, str>,

The 4-line rationale lives in one place; new variants get a one-line pointer comment.

This is a readability finding: a contributor reading just Error::ProfileViolation has the rationale right there, but a contributor reading both variants gets the same paragraph twice and may suspect the second copy is subtly different. It is not.
title: Cow<'static, str> rationale comment for ProfileViolation.reason duplicated across two variants; should hoist to one place
